children: reported third-quarter sales of $22.8 billion, up 9.3%, and shares fell 5.43% to $208.50 in premarket trading at 8:58 a.m. ET on November 18. The home improvement retailer's results came a day after rival Home Depot reported its own quarter and named a new chief executive.

Comparable sales rose 1.8%, the sixth straight quarterly gain, and online sales climbed 17.4%. Adjusted EPS increased 1.3% to $3.10, but about $250 million of pre-tax tariff refunds added $0.34 per share. Gross margin narrowed to 32.95% from 34.19% and operating margin slipped to 11.32% from 11.92%. Lowe's raised its fiscal 2026 sales outlook to about $92.5 billion and comparable sales to about 0.5%, but cut its adjusted operating margin outlook to about 11.5% from 11.6%, with adjusted EPS of about $12.25, Investing.com reported alongside the premarket move.

Stripping out the refund, adjusted EPS would have been about $2.76 against $3.06 a year earlier, a decline of nearly 10%. The gap between 9.3% sales growth and 1.8% comparable sales suggests acquired businesses are doing much of the top-line work. At about 17 times the $12.25 full-year guide, the multiple is moderate. GuruFocus gives Lowe's a GF Score of 81/100, built on strong profitability with a middling balance sheet. Its GF Value of $255.05 puts the premarket price about 18% below the model, which GuruFocus rates modestly undervalued, but that gap may hold until margins stabilize. The next test is fourth-quarter gross margin, without refund help.

title: Lowe's Stocks Fall 5.43% Premarket as Tariff Refund Masks Margin Squeeze
